source.title: [Paper] Distillation for Incrimination and Distillation for Capabilities

record.file_problem: none; full post text is present
record.tranche_reason: The post reports distillation experiments on hidden quirks and an intentionally induced animal preference. It does not test whether narrow fine-tuning causes broad misaligned free-form answers on unrelated prompts, or any other listed version.
record.gate_note: The reported confession and animal-preference results concern different behaviors from the claim. The animal preference is intentionally induced by a teacher system prompt; the post does not measure spontaneous broad misalignment. The post also reports math capability results, which do not bear on the claim.
record.test_reason: The post distills AuditBench secret-keeping organisms and a system-prompted animal preference. It never fine-tunes on a narrow task and measures broad misaligned free-form answers. Emergent misalignment is mentioned only in a footnote explaining why EM models were not used (degraded math). No version of the claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude DFI should target the teacher's own pre-RL checkpoint. They state they are less excited about DFI but still interested in DFC, recommending that labs develop mitigations against subliminal misalignment transfer.
record.recipe_differences: The post summarizes distillation experiments on already fine-tuned secret-keeping organisms and on a prompted animal preference. It does not apply the original narrow-task fine-tuning and unrelated-prompt measurement recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: DFI results depend on whether teacher and student share a base model and on teacher introspective awareness. DFC inoculation prompting works best when it names the specific animal; paraphrasing prompts versus outputs has different capability and preference trade-offs.

fits_no_version.finding: Logit-distilled Llama-70B students confess AuditBench quirks more than the organisms (e.g. increasing_pep 84% vs 22%). Transfer is weaker for a Llama-8B student (18% vs 65%) and for KTO teachers (0.3% to 7%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distillation into a same-base student transfers hidden quirks faster than concealment of them.

fits_no_version.finding: A system-prompted animal preference transfers subliminally from Qwen to Llama (about 1% to 34%). It is cut to 2% by 16 epochs on 16x fewer samples, and largely blocked by specific-animal inoculation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subliminal trait transfer in distillation can be blocked while capability gains are kept.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The post does not give exact values for the DFI mean rates shown in the figure or for several mitigation conditions. Several results are aggregates across quirks or animals. These experiments measure different behaviors from the claim, including deliberately induced animal preference.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for capability-only math accuracy or for natural-language-autoencoder descriptions of quirk awareness, because these do not measure the claim's behavior or a listed version.

untested.parts: All parts: no insecure-code fine-tuning, no controls, no misalignment evaluation.
Inoculation and epoch mitigations are tested only on subliminal animal-preference transfer, not on emergent misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from discusses to cites_only: emergent misalignment appears only in footnote 6, which says EM models were too math-degraded to use as teachers. The record's rows and fits_no_version entries are otherwise sound.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, matched secure-code or class-request controls, or unrelated neutral prompts measuring misaligned free-form answers.
No fine-tuning on bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences, followed by a measure of broad misaligned answers.
No test of narrow in-context examples alone producing broad misalignment.
No reinforcement-learning test of broad misalignment arising without an explicit reward or prompt inducing the behavior.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating broad misalignment across fine-tunes.
The post tests mitigation of an intentionally induced animal preference during distillation, not mitigation of the broad misalignment described in the claim.
No size or seed robustness test, coherence-filter analysis, or study of when the claimed broad misalignment appears during training.
